sections.title: 1. The Sovereign & Legislative Dual Role of the Assembly

masteryZone.q: Who presided over the Constituent Assembly when it met as a legislative body to enact ordinary laws?
opts: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
G.V. Mavalankar
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
Jawaharlal Nehru
masteryZone.sol: G.V. Mavalankar presided as Speaker during legislative sessions.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following acts officially declared the Constituent Assembly to be a fully sovereign body?
opts: Cabinet Mission Plan 1946
Indian Independence Act 1947
Government of India Act 1935
Charter Act of 1833
masteryZone.sol: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 granted full sovereign status to the Assembly.

masteryZone.q: What was the date of the first legislative session of the Constituent Assembly?
opts: December 9, 1946
August 15, 1947
November 17, 1947
January 26, 1950
masteryZone.sol: It first met as the Dominion Legislature on November 17, 1947.

masteryZone.q: The dual functions of the Constituent Assembly were performed on:
opts: The same day in separate chambers
Separate days under different presiding officers
Alternate months under a single president
Sundays only
masteryZone.sol: The constituent and legislative functions were performed on separate days under different presiding officers.

masteryZone.q: Who was the president of the Constituent Assembly when it performed its constituent function?
opts: G.V. Mavalankar
Dr. Rajendra Prasad
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
masteryZone.sol: Dr. Rajendra Prasad presided when it met as a constituent body to frame the Constitution.

masteryZone.q: Identify the two distinct functions assigned to the Constituent Assembly post-independence: (Select all that apply)
opts: Framing the Constitution of India
Enacting ordinary laws for the country
Conducting general elections
Negotiating trade treaties with European nations
masteryZone.sol: The Assembly had dual functions: making of the Constitution (constituent) and enacting ordinary laws (legislative).

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are correct regarding G.V. Mavalankar's role in the Assembly? (Select all that apply)
opts: He presided over the Assembly as a legislative body.
He was elected as the Speaker of the Dominion Legislature.
He chaired the Drafting Committee.
He presided over the first legislative session on November 17, 1947.
masteryZone.sol: He presided as Speaker over legislative sessions, starting November 17, 1947. He did not chair the Drafting Committee (which was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar).

masteryZone.q: What did the sovereign status of the Constituent Assembly mean? (Select all that apply)
opts: It could alter or abrogate any previous British laws concerning India.
It could frame any constitution it pleased.
It was completely free from the Cabinet Mission Plan constraints.
It was subject to a veto by the British Crown.
masteryZone.sol: Sovereignty meant complete freedom from British constraints, including the power to rewrite British laws and make any constitution, free of royal veto.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following bodies acted as legislatures of India during the transition phase (1947-1952)? (Select all that apply)
opts: The Constituent Assembly of India (Dominion Legislature)
The provisional Parliament of India
The Imperial Legislative Council
The House of Lords
masteryZone.sol: The Constituent Assembly functioned as the Dominion Legislature and later as the provisional Parliament of India.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are true about the dual presidencies in the Assembly? (Select all that apply)
opts: Dr. Rajendra Prasad presided over constituent sessions.
G.V. Mavalankar presided over legislative sessions.
Both Prasad and Mavalankar presided on the same day.
The presidencies were rotated on a weekly basis.
masteryZone.sol: Prasad and Mavalankar presided over separate constituent and legislative sessions on separate days.

masteryZone.q: The Constituent Assembly of India was fully sovereign from its very first meeting on December 9, 1946.
masteryZone.sol: False. It became sovereign only on August 15, 1947, via the Indian Independence Act of 1947.

masteryZone.q: Dr. Rajendra Prasad presided over both constituent and legislative sessions of the Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: False. G.V. Mavalankar presided over legislative sessions.

masteryZone.q: The Assembly performed its constituent and legislative functions on separate days.
masteryZone.sol: True. This avoided confusion of roles.

masteryZone.q: The provisional Parliament of India functioned until the first general elections were held in 1951-52.
masteryZone.sol: True. It was replaced by the newly elected Parliament in April 1952.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 allowed the Assembly to repeal the Independence Act itself.
masteryZone.sol: True. As a sovereign body, it could repeal or alter any British law concerning India.

masteryZone.q: The legislative role of the Assembly ended on November 26, 1949.
masteryZone.sol: False. The constituent role ended then, but it continued to function as provisional Parliament until 1952.

masteryZone.q: The British Crown retained the power to veto laws passed by the Dominion Legislature after August 15, 1947.
masteryZone.sol: False. Veto power was transferred to the Governor-General of the Dominion.

masteryZone.q: G.V. Mavalankar was elected as the Speaker of the Dominion Legislature on November 17, 1947.
masteryZone.sol: True. This was the first legislative meeting.

masteryZone.q: The Constituent Assembly met for the first time as the Dominion Legislature on November 17, ___________.
masteryZone.sol: It met as the Dominion Legislature on November 17, 1947.

masteryZone.q: When the Assembly met as a legislative body, it was presided over by G.V. ___________.
masteryZone.sol: G.V. Mavalankar presided as Speaker.

masteryZone.q: When the Assembly met to frame the Constitution, it was presided over by Dr. Rajendra ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Dr. Rajendra Prasad presided over constituent sessions.

masteryZone.q: The sovereign status of the Assembly was granted by the Indian ___________ Act of 1947.
masteryZone.sol: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 granted this status.

masteryZone.q: The dual functions of the Assembly were performed on ___________ days.
masteryZone.sol: They were conducted on separate days to avoid mixing roles.

masteryZone.q: The constituent function of the Assembly was completed on November 26, ___________.
masteryZone.sol: The Constitution was adopted on November 26, 1949.

masteryZone.q: After adopting the Constitution, the Assembly acted as the ___________ Parliament until elections.
masteryZone.sol: It functioned as the provisional Parliament of India.

masteryZone.q: Under the 1947 Act, the Governor-General had full power to give ___________ to any law in the name of His Majesty.
masteryZone.sol: He could give assent to laws on behalf of the British Crown.

masteryZone.q: Match the Assembly functions with their presiding officers and tasks:

options.text: A. Presided by Dr. Rajendra Prasad to frame the Constitution
B. Presided by G.V. Mavalankar to pass ordinary laws
C. Chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to draft clauses

masteryZone.sol: Options match directly (I-A, II-B, III-C).

masteryZone.q: Match the key dates of transition with their significance:

options.text: A. Indian Independence and sovereignty of Assembly
B. First legislative meeting under G.V. Mavalankar
C. Adoption of the Constitution and end of dual function

masteryZone.sol: Options match directly (I-A, II-B, III-C).

masteryZone.q: Match the terms with their legal definitions under the 1947 Act:

options.text: A. Power to alter or abrogate any British law
B. Capacity to enact ordinary federal laws
C. Continuous legislative role of Assembly from 1950 to 1952

masteryZone.sol: Options match directly (I-A, II-B, III-C).

masteryZone.q: Which body became the first Parliament of independent India?
masteryZone.sol: The Constituent Assembly of India (in its legislative capacity).

masteryZone.q: Who was the first Speaker of the Dominion Legislature of free India?
masteryZone.sol: G.V. Mavalankar.

masteryZone.q: Who presided when the Assembly met to draft the Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: Dr. Rajendra Prasad.

masteryZone.q: Under which plan was the Constituent Assembly originally set up in 1946?
masteryZone.sol: The Cabinet Mission Plan.

masteryZone.q: When did the Constituent Assembly adopt the Constitution of India?
masteryZone.sol: November 26, 1949.

masteryZone.q: How were the constituent and legislative capacities of the Assembly separated?
masteryZone.sol: By conducting them on separate days under different presiding officers.

masteryZone.q: What was the legislative status of the Assembly between 1950 and 1952?
masteryZone.sol: It functioned as the provisional Parliament of India.

masteryZone.q: Did the British Crown retain the power of reservation of bills after August 15, 1947?
masteryZone.sol: No, the right of veto or reservation of bills by the Crown was abolished.

masteryZone.q:

2. It adopted the Constitution on November 26, 1949.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct, describing legislative session start and adoption of constitution.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Assembly was a fully sovereign body under the Cabinet Mission Plan.
2. The Independence Act of 1947 abolished the sovereignty of the Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are false. The Assembly was non-sovereign under the Cabinet Mission Plan, and became sovereign under the 1947 Act.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Dr. Rajendra Prasad presided over the constituent sessions.
2. G.V. Mavalankar presided over the legislative sessions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct, explaining the dual presidencies.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the provisional Parliament:
1. It was established immediately on August 15, 1947.
2. It functioned until the first general elections in 1951-52.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect because the Assembly functioned as the Dominion Legislature initially, and became the provisional Parliament on January 26, 1950.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the legislative powers post-1947:
1. The Assembly required British parliamentary approval to pass laws.
2. Royal veto power over dominion laws was abolished.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect because the Assembly was fully sovereign.

masteryZone.q: Why was the Constituent Assembly given legislative powers in 1947?
masteryZone.sol: Because with independence, the old central legislature dissolved, and the Assembly had to act as the interim Parliament to pass ordinary federal laws and prevent a governance vacuum.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Assembly perform its dual functions on separate days?
masteryZone.sol: To ensure clear separation of roles between framing the fundamental law of the land (constitution-making) and passing day-to-day ordinary laws (legislative capacity).

masteryZone.q: Why was the sovereign character of the Assembly critical?
masteryZone.sol: It allowed the Assembly to frame a constitution suited to Indian needs, free from British dictates, with the legal authority to rewrite or repeal previous colonial acts.

masteryZone.q: How did the 1947 Act change the legal status of the Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: It transformed the Assembly from a non-sovereign body limited by British rules into a fully sovereign legislature with supreme authority over Indian laws.

masteryZone.q: How did G.V. Mavalankar's role differ from Dr. Rajendra Prasad's?
masteryZone.sol: Mavalankar presided over sessions enacting ordinary laws (Dominion Legislature), whereas Prasad presided over sessions drafting the Constitution.

masteryZone.q: How did the Assembly function as the provisional Parliament after 1950?
masteryZone.sol: It continued to enact ordinary laws under the new Constitution until the first general elections were completed and a new bicameral Parliament was formed in 1952.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: In November 1947, the Assembly sat as a legislative body to debate ordinary bills. Why was G.V. Mavalankar chosen to preside instead of Dr. Rajendra Prasad?
masteryZone.sol: To establish parliamentary protocol. As the legislative body functioned like a parliament, G.V. Mavalankar was elected Speaker to lead legislative debates, while Dr. Prasad remained the President of the constituent body.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Assembly passed the Representation of the People Act, 1950, before the first general elections. What does this case study reveal about the Assembly's powers?
masteryZone.sol: It reveals that the Assembly possessed complete legislative authority to pass complex organic laws necessary to prepare the nation for democracy.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Under the Cabinet Mission, the Assembly had no power to change the basic structure without British assent. How did the Act of 1947 break this deadlock?
masteryZone.sol: By granting full sovereignty, it enabled the Assembly to override all previous limitations, rewrite any constitutional clauses, and ignore British cabinet control.

masteryZone.q: Explain the dual-role system of the Constituent Assembly post-1947 to a beginner.
masteryZone.sol: Post-1947, the Assembly had two separate jobs: making the Constitution (presided by Dr. Rajendra Prasad) and passing ordinary laws (presided by Speaker G.V. Mavalankar). They did these jobs on separate days to keep the roles clear.

masteryZone.q: Explain what made the Constituent Assembly 'sovereign' after August 15, 1947.
masteryZone.sol: Sovereignty meant that the Assembly was the supreme law-making authority, free from any British controls, and could rewrite, modify, or repeal any previous British laws concerning India.

masteryZone.q: Explain the significance of G.V. Mavalankar's election in the Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: It marked the beginning of independent India's parliamentary tradition. By electing him Speaker of the legislative sessions, the Assembly established the distinct office of the Speaker, separate from the head of the constituent body.

masteryZone.q: Following partition, the total strength of the Constituent Assembly of India fell from 389 to:
masteryZone.sol: The total strength fell to 299 due to the withdrawal of Muslim League members representing areas included in Pakistan.

masteryZone.q: What was the post-partition representation of the Indian Provinces (formerly British Provinces) in the Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: The representation of provinces fell to 229.

masteryZone.q: The representation of Indian Princely States in the Constituent Assembly fell from 93 to:
masteryZone.sol: Princely state membership was reduced to 70.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 declared that British paramountcy over the Princely States would:
opts: Be transferred to the Dominion of India
Be transferred to the Dominion of Pakistan
Lapse on August 15, 1947
Be maintained by British troops
masteryZone.sol: British paramountcy over princely states lapsed on August 15, 1947, leaving them free to join either dominion or remain independent.

masteryZone.q: Which office in England was abolished by the Indian Independence Act of 1947?
opts: Viceroy of India
Secretary of State for India
Prime Minister of Great Britain
Governor-General of India
masteryZone.sol: The office of the Secretary of State for India was abolished, and its functions were transferred to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Relations.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following changes occurred in the composition of the Assembly due to partition? (Select all that apply)
opts: The total strength fell to 299.
The provincial membership fell to 229.
The princely states' membership fell to 70.
The Muslim League members from East Bengal withdrew.
masteryZone.sol: All listed statements are correct composition changes post-partition.

masteryZone.q: Which territories' representatives withdrew from the Constituent Assembly of India to join Pakistan's Assembly? (Select all that apply)
opts: East Bengal
West Punjab
Sindh and Baluchistan
Madras and Bombay
masteryZone.sol: Representatives of East Bengal, West Punjab, Sindh, Baluchistan, and Sylhet withdrew. Madras and Bombay remained in India.

masteryZone.q: What was the legal status of the Princely States after the Indian Independence Act of 1947? (Select all that apply)
opts: They were freed from British paramountcy.
They could choose to join the Dominion of India.
They could choose to join the Dominion of Pakistan.
They were forced to remain independent.
masteryZone.sol: Paramountcy lapsed, leaving states free to join India, Pakistan, or remain independent (though most joined India).

masteryZone.q: Which of the following offices or titles were dropped or modified by the Act of 1947? (Select all that apply)
opts: The title of 'Emperor of India' from the British Royal style
The office of the Secretary of State for India
The office of the Governor-General of India
The office of the Viceroy of India
masteryZone.sol: The title of Emperor was dropped, Secretary of State was abolished, and Viceroy was replaced by a constitutional Governor-General. The Governor-General office itself was not abolished.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are true about the provincial representation post-partition? (Select all that apply)
opts: The highest representation was from the United Provinces.
Madras had the second highest representation.
The representation fell from 296 to 229.
Bombay's representation fell to zero.
masteryZone.sol: United Provinces had 55, Madras had 49, and total fell from 296 to 229. Bombay remained in India.

masteryZone.q: The withdrawal of the Muslim League members led to a reduction in the Assembly's strength to 299.
masteryZone.sol: True. League members representing Pakistan withdrew.

masteryZone.q: The post-partition representation of the Indian Provinces fell to 229.
masteryZone.sol: True. It fell from 296 to 229.

masteryZone.q: The Princely States had a final strength of 93 members in the restructured Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: False. It fell from 93 to 70.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 declared that British paramountcy over Indian states lapsed.
masteryZone.sol: True. All treaties and paramountcy lapsed on August 15, 1947.

masteryZone.q: The office of the Secretary of State for India was maintained but made subordinate to the Governor-General.
masteryZone.sol: False. The office was completely abolished.

masteryZone.q: The British monarch continued to hold the title of 'Emperor of India' after August 15, 1947.
masteryZone.sol: False. The title was dropped from the royal style.

masteryZone.q: The Act of 1947 allowed the Princely States to remain independent if they chose not to join either dominion.
masteryZone.sol: True. Though most joined India due to geographical and political realities.

masteryZone.q: The boundary commission post-partition was headed by Sir Stafford Cripps.
masteryZone.sol: False. It was headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe.

masteryZone.q: The withdrawal of the Muslim League members reduced the Assembly's total strength to ___________.

masteryZone.q: The number of representatives from Indian Provinces fell from 296 to ___________.
masteryZone.sol: It fell to 229.

masteryZone.q: The membership of the Princely States fell from 93 to ___________.
masteryZone.sol: It fell to 70.

masteryZone.q: The Act of 1947 declared the lapse of British ___________ over the Princely States.
masteryZone.sol: British paramountcy over the states lapsed on August 15, 1947.

masteryZone.q: The functions of the Secretary of State for India were transferred to the Secretary of State for ___________ Relations.
masteryZone.sol: They were transferred to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Relations.

masteryZone.q: The British monarch dropped the title of ___________ of India.
masteryZone.sol: The title 'Emperor of India' was dropped.

masteryZone.q: The partition of Bengal and Punjab was carried out under the June ___________ Plan.
masteryZone.sol: It was based on the June 3 Plan (Mountbatten Plan).

masteryZone.q: The Boundary Commission was headed by Sir Cyril ___________.
masteryZone.sol: It was headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding partition plans:
1. Partition was carried out under the Cabinet Mission Plan.
2. The Mountbatten Plan was announced on June 3, 1947.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect because partition was carried out under the Mountbatten Plan.

masteryZone.q:

2. It demarcated borders for Bengal and Punjab.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct.

masteryZone.q: Why did the membership of the Princely States fall from 93 to 70?
masteryZone.sol: Because partition resulted in some princely states falling within the geographic boundaries of Pakistan, meaning their representatives withdrew from the Indian Assembly.

masteryZone.q: Why was the office of the Secretary of State for India abolished?
masteryZone.sol: Because with independence, the British Crown surrendered all political and administrative authority over India, making a colonial cabinet minister redundant.

masteryZone.q: Why was the Government of India Act 1935 used as the interim constitution?
masteryZone.sol: To provide a stable, pre-existing administrative and legal framework to run the country's daily governance until the new Constitution was completed and adopted.

masteryZone.q: How did partition affect the representation of British Provinces?
masteryZone.sol: It reduced their representation from 296 to 229 as the provincial territories of East Bengal, West Punjab, Sindh, Baluchistan, and Sylhet joined Pakistan.

masteryZone.q: How did the lapse of British paramountcy affect the Princely States?
masteryZone.sol: It freed them from British treaties, allowing them to choose between joining India, joining Pakistan, or remaining independent.

masteryZone.q: How were provincial representation numbers allocated in the restructured Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: They were allocated in proportion to the population of the provinces remaining within the new borders of India.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The province of East Bengal had a large representation in the original Assembly of 1946. Why did all its members withdraw in 1947?
masteryZone.sol: Because partition allocated East Bengal to Pakistan, and its representatives withdrew to form the separate Constituent Assembly of Pakistan.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: In 1948, the Government of India used the modified Government of India Act 1935 to manage a trade dispute. What was the constitutional basis for this?
masteryZone.sol: Section 8 of the Indian Independence Act of 1947, which mandated using the modified 1935 Act as the interim constitution during the transition.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Hyderabad princely state did not send representatives to the Constituent Assembly in 1946. How did the lapse of paramountcy in 1947 affect its options?
masteryZone.sol: It made Hyderabad technically independent, creating a complex integration challenge that was eventually resolved via military action (Operation Polo) in 1948.

masteryZone.q: Explain why the total strength of the Constituent Assembly fell from 389 to 299.
masteryZone.sol: Due to the partition of British India, the areas of East Bengal, West Punjab, Sindh, Baluchistan, and Sylhet joined Pakistan. The Muslim League members representing these areas withdrew, reducing the strength.

masteryZone.q: Explain the lapse of British paramountcy over the Princely States.
masteryZone.sol: Lapse of paramountcy meant that all treaties and agreements between the British Crown and the princely states ended. The states were no longer under British protection or control and were free to join India, Pakistan, or remain independent.

masteryZone.q: Explain how the government of India operated during the transition phase (1947-1950).
masteryZone.sol: It operated under the modified Government of India Act 1935 as the interim constitution, with the Governor-General as the nominal head and the Constituent Assembly acting as the supreme legislature until the new Constitution was adopted.
